sources.title: London Plan Evidence
sources.verified_claim: City Hall lists March-July 2026 economy evidence including the London Employment Sites Database, employment projections and economic/infrastructure supply-demand work. Evidence-base inclusion is not an exact parcel allocation or deliverability result.

sources.title: London Industrial Land Supply Study
sources.published_at: updated 2026 current page; study 2023 with 2025 update
sources.verified_claim: The GLA study reviews industrial-land quantity, SIL functions and theoretical intensification potential and states it is a high-level starting point for further local evidence. It is not parcel-specific availability or permission evidence.

sources.title: Strategic Industrial Land (SIL)
sources.published_at: 2026 current dataset; last update seven months before crawl
sources.verified_claim: GLA publishes SIL GIS polygons and explicitly labels boundaries indicative, advising users to contact the relevant borough to confirm accuracy. No candidate SIL intersection is asserted without canonical spatial matching and borough confirmation.

sources.title: 4. Growing London’s economy in a way that benefits all
sources.verified_claim: The Draft London Plan chapter includes policies on employment space and industrial land supply. Draft status is retained and the policies are not silently treated as adopted development-plan constraints.

sources.title: Evidence base
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's evidence page links its 2024 Employment Land Review and states the emerging plan seeks industrial and town-centre office floorspace through 2041. Borough need figures do not establish parcel_30762 employment use or deliverability.

sources.title: Local Plan update
sources.verified_claim: Havering's Local Plan update publishes a new Employment Land Review and cluster summaries as evidence for future employment land provision. Evidence-base status is not a parcel_46142 allocation or permission.

sources.title: Business and Jobs
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's evidence register includes KIBA, industrial-land, office and workspace studies with mixed publication ages. Source age is retained and no parcel_61522 employment capacity is inferred.

sources.title: Preview of London employment projections (2024-based update)
sources.verified_claim: GLA Economics previews 2025-2050 employment projections using data available to end-2024 and describes central and sensitivity scenarios. Long-term job projections are not a commitment that a sample parcel will receive employment floorspace or tenants.
